statement: A circle has centre $C(2,3)$ and passes through $P(5,7)$. (i) Find its radius and equation. (ii) Find the equation of the tangent at $P$. (iii) Find where this tangent meets the line $x=0$. (iv) Show that the tangent is perpendicular to the radius $CP$ by verifying that the product of their gradients is $-1$.
solution: (i) $r^{2}=(5-2)^{2}+(7-3)^{2}=9+16=25$, so $r=5$ and $(x-2)^{2}+(y-3)^{2}=25$. (ii) Radius $CP$ has gradient $\frac{7-3}{5-2}=\frac43$, so tangent gradient is $-\frac34$. Tangent: $y-7=-\frac34(x-5)$. (iii) At $x=0$: $y=7+\frac{15}{4}=\frac{43}{4}$. Point $(0,\frac{43}{4})$. (iv) Gradient of radius $CP$ is $\frac43$ and gradient of tangent is $-\frac34$; their product is $\frac43\cdot(-\frac34)=-1$, confirming perpendicularity.
hints: Use the distance formula for the radius.
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
